name: Front Range Pipeline (PSCo)
researcher_notes: The line is not in the roster under any name. Existing Colorado rows are Colorado Interstate Gas, TransColorado, and a Mexico line, none of which is this pipe. The EIA pipeline projects release for August 2026, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 103, lists Front Range Expansion by Public Service Co of CO: completed November 1998, Colorado, 53 miles, 24 inches, 269 MMcf/d added, cost 25.1 million dollars, interstate, FERC docket CP98-49. The cost is staged as 25100000 USD. A Federal Register notice from April 16, 1998 confirms Public Service Company of Colorado applied to the Colorado Public Utilities Commission in December 1997 to build the Front Range Pipeline. That notice does not state length or capacity. A web search summary of a 1998 Natural Gas Intelligence article gave the same 53 miles, 24 inches and 269,000 dekatherms, Chalk Bluffs Hub near the Colorado-Wyoming border to near Fort St. Vrain, built through WYCO Development LLC (a Public Service and Colorado Interstate Gas alliance), about 25 million dollars. That article page could not be loaded, so it is not cited. Endpoints are therefore left in notes only. A separate 2001 EIA project, CIG Front Range Expansion (FERC CP01-1, 24 in, 58 miles), is a different Colorado Interstate Gas project and should be checked against that system before staging. Owner name matches the ownership team spelling exactly. Capacity is the 1998 incremental figure, so treat as approximate. Only one validated source states the values, which suffices. Route not researched. Length is 85 km, above the 25 km threshold, and the line is in service, so the concrete-step test is met.
